"''Sir.|Lieutenant Endicott and Jad Bean|audio=Endicott-Bean-ROTJ.flac |}} '''Endicott''' was a [[human]] who served as a [[lieutenant]] in the [[Galactic Empire]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. In [[4 ABY]], Endicott was stationed on the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]] [[superweapon]] and oversaw the arrival of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader's]] [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] [[ST 321]]. As Vader landed, the lieutenant gave the order for the station's [[commander]], [[Moff]] [[Tiaan Jerjerrod]], to be alerted to the new arrival. He was later present on the [[Death Star]]'s [[Overbridge (Death Star II)|Overbridge]] when it first fired upon the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] during the [[Battle of Endor]] and ultimately perished when the [[battle station]] was destroyed. ==Biography== ===Vader's arrival=== {{Quote|Command station, this is ST-321, code clearance blue. We are starting our approach. Deactivate the security shield.''"
"''The security deflector shield will be deactivated when we have confirmation of your code transmission. Stand by.|Captain Yorr and Jad Bean|audio=Yorr-Bean-ROTJ.flac|}} [[File:Endicott_oversees.png|thumb|right|300px|alt=Endicott stands over a trio of Death Star controllers including Jad Bean in a hangar command room. Another controller stands in a raised console behind the group.|Endicott oversaw the arrival of Darth Vader on board the Death Star II.]] The [[human]] Endicott served as a [[lieutenant]] in the [[Imperial Officer Corps]] of the [[Galactic Empire]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] fought against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. In [[4 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|VI}} to [[4 ABY]]. he was stationed on board the [[superweapon]] known as the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]] while it was under construction in [[orbit]] above the [[forest]] [[moon]] [[Endor]]. The lieutenant was overseeing{{Film|VI}} {{AD|Disney+}} one of the [[battle station]]'s [[hangar]]s from an overlooking command room when the [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] "[[ST 321]]," carrying the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], began its approach to the [[Death Star]]. The lieutenant watched over the shoulder of station monitor [[Jad Bean]]''[[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]]'' as he confirmed the [[shuttle]]'s code clearance and then deactivated a hangar's [[deflector shield]] so that the [[starship]] could enter. Endicott then monitored the shuttle entering the hangar before briskly turning his head to order Bean to inform [[Moff]] [[Tiaan Jerjerrod]], [[commander]] of the Death Star, of [[Sith Lord|Lord]] Vader's arrival. Jerjerrod then greeted Vader personally as the [[Sith]] disembarked his shuttle. ===Battle of Endor=== {{Quote|Fire!|Jerjerrod orders the Death Star II to fire on the Alliance Fleet as Endicott watches|audio=Jerjerrod-Fire-ROTJ.flac|}} [[File:Jerjerrod_and_Endicott.png|thumb|left|300px|alt=Endicott stands beside a station manned by Jad Bean on the Death Star Overbridge as Jerjerrod gives the order for the Death Star to fire on the ''Liberty''.|Endicott witnessed Jerjerrod give the order for the Death Star II to fire its first shot in the Battle of Endor.]] The Death Star was later [[Battle of Endor|attacked]] by the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]], who believed that the station was vulnerable as it was not yet fully operational. This was untrue however, as the rebels had been purposefully deceived as part of [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine's]] plan to lure them into a trap. During the battle, Endicott was present in the Death Star's [[Overbridge (Death Star II)|Overbridge]] when Jerjerrod gave the order for the Death Star's fully functional [[superlaser]] to fire its first shot at the rebel fleet, destroying the [[MC80 Star Cruiser]] ''[[Liberty]]''.''[[Lost Stars]]'' Despite being unprepared to face the superlaser, the rebels ultimately managed to turn the tide of the battle in their favor after a [[Endor strike team|strike team]] on Endor managed to destroy the [[Endor shield generator bunker|bunker]] generating the Death Star's shields. Endicott was [[Death|killed]] when the superweapon was destroyed. ==Personality and traits== Endicott had light skin, [[Color|brown]] [[hair]], and blue [[eye]]s. ==Skills and abilities== Endicott had slightly above average intelligence and [[diplomat]]ic skills, average speed, and slightly below average strength and fighting ability. He was not [[Force-sensitive]]. ==Equipment== Endicott wore a black [[Imperial military uniforms|Imperial officer's uniform]] including a [[Hat|cap]] and a silver [[utility belt]]. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|It was a fantastic experience, very nice, seriously professional. Quite quiet, the set. There wasn't a lot of sort of banter. They were very focused, because I think what they were doing, technically, was really quite hard. I think the lighting and that kind of thing was really acute. I'll say it was incredibly dark. So, you'll sort of be in the darkness with people with torches, you know, coming up and whispering to you. And then, suddenly, a couple of lights would go on, and it was a bit like being on the Death Star, you know, I guess.|Glyn Baker|{{YouTube|video=wLiHCysBXkc|text=Glyn Baker Interview - 002 The Living Daylights, Star Wars Return of The Jedi & The Wild Geese|channel=@FlicksAndTheCity|name=Flicks And The City|quote=Glyn Baker interview about playing 002 on The Living Daylights, Lt Endcott on the set of Star Wars Return of the Jedi & his first film The Wild Geese. Glyn also chats about Star Wars Episodes 7, 8 & 9 and the 50th James Bond anniversary.}} [[Wookieepedia:Interview/Endicott/Glyn Baker interview transcript|transcript]].}} [[File:ScrewYouStormies-ROTJBR.jpg|thumb|left|300px|alt=A frame from a deleted scene showing Endicott stood beside Jerjerrod on the Death Star Overbridge, with Jad Bean stood in a raised console behind them.|Endicott appeared in several additional scenes on the Death Star II Overbridge that were deleted from ''Return of the Jedi''.]] In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Endicott first appeared in the [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], which released on [[May 25]], [[1983]].''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' The character was portrayed uncredited by [[Glyn Baker]] with all Endicott's scenes filmed on Stage 7 of [[Elstree Studios]] on [[April 1]], [[1982]], the last day of main stage shooting for the film in the [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]].''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]'' Baker did not know what his role would be until he arrived on set and found the shoot relatively quiet and often dark, requiring the use of torches. Aside from the two scenes including Endicott in the film, Baker also shot additional scenes on the Overbridge that were cut. In the first scene, Endicott is stood overlooking a group of [[controller]]s when Palpatine contacts Jerjerrod and orders{{HomeVideoCite|set=Star Wars: The Complete Saga|scene=Jerjerrod's Conflict|nolink=1}} him to destroy Endor if the shield bunker is destroyed. In the second scene, Endicott informs Jerjerrod of the destruction of the bunker on Endor, prompting the Moff to order the Death Star to destroy Endor itself. Endicott then relays these orders to those stationed in the room. The character speaks with a [[Wikipedia:British English|British accent]] in this scene, differing from the [[Wikipedia:American English|American accent]] the character uses in scenes included in the film. [[File:GlynBaker.png|thumb|right|300px|alt=Glyn Baker at a fan convention.|Endicott was portrayed by Glyn Baker.]] In the current canon, the character was first named on a card in the ''[[2018 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files]]'' set of trading cards released by [[Topps|The Topps Company, Inc.]] In the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, [[Endicott/Legends|Endicott]] first appeared prior to the release of the film in its [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]] by [[James Kahn]],[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]] which was released on [[May 12]], 1983. The character was then first identified as Endicott on a card in the [[2000]] ''[[Death Star II Limited]]'' expansion set of the ''[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]]''.{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Lieutenant Endicott}} ==Appearances== {{Indexpage}} {{Mediacat|soundcat=Audio files of Endicott|imagecat=Images of Endicott}} *{{Film|VI}} {{1st}} *[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (paperback novel)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]] *''[[Return of the Jedi - The Film Novel]]'' ==Sources== *''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi]]'' {{BtsOnly}} *''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]'' {{BtsOnly}} *''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' {{BtsOnly}} *''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]'' {{BtsOnly}} *{{Topps|set=2016 Topps Star Wars: Rogue One Mission Briefing|cardname=Glyn Baker as Lieutenant Endicott|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/137403/cid/11208700/2016-Topps-Star-Wars-Rogue-One:-Mission-Briefing---Autographs-NNO-Glyn-Baker}} {{1stID|Endicott}} *{{Topps|set=2018 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files|cardname=ROTJ-27 - Lieutenant Endicott|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/170092/cid/11689265/2018-Topps-Star-Wars-Galactic-Files-ROTJ-27-Lieutenant-Endicott}} *''[[Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'' *{{SWCT|set=2020 Base Series 2|cardname=Lieutenant Endicott}} *{{EncyclopediaCite|Imperial Troops}} {{Po}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |es=Endicott }} [[Category:Humans]] [[Category:Individuals of unspecified gender]] [[Category:Individuals with he/him pronouns]] [[Category:Officers of the Galactic Empire]]
